sections.1.heading: What online billing and invoicing software actually changes
sections.1.paragraphs: Online billing and invoicing software runs in a web browser. There's nothing to install, and your data sits in one account instead of on one person's computer. That sounds like a small detail until the person who keeps the invoicing spreadsheet goes on holiday at the end of the month. | For a team that bills hours, the bigger change is that time and invoices live in the same place. Everyone tracks their hours into the same account during the month. When it's time to bill, the person doing the invoicing doesn't have to chase timesheets by email or merge three versions of a file. The unbilled hours are already there, priced at the rates you set for each project and task. | It also means there's one history per client. Every invoice you've sent, what's been paid and what's still open sit together, so anyone with the right access can answer a client's question without digging through a shared drive.
sections.1.bullets: Nothing to install: open Paidlyo in a web browser and sign in | One shared account for the whole team's hours | Unbilled time is ready to invoice, with no timesheets to collect by email | One history per client: invoices, payments and open balances
sections.1.callout: If your invoices still depend on one file on one laptop, that file is a single point of failure for your cash flow.
sections.2.heading: Sending an invoice as a link instead of an attachment
sections.2.paragraphs: In Paidlyo each invoice has a private client link. Your client opens it in a browser and sees the invoice straight away, with no account and no password. If their finance team needs a file for their records, they can save it as a PDF from the same page. | A link has a few advantages over a PDF attached to an email. It's small, so it doesn't get stuck in a spam filter for its size. It also shows the invoice exactly as you finished it, so nobody is working from an older copy you sent last week. | You still send the link yourself, from your own email or the chat tool your client uses. That's a good thing: a short personal note from you is more likely to be read than an automated message from a system the client doesn't know.
sections.2.bullets: Put the invoice number and amount in the subject line | Add the client's purchase order number or reference if they gave you one | Say when payment is due and how they can pay you | Send it to the person who approves invoices, not only to your day-to-day contact
sections.2.callout: Ask a new client who approves invoices before you send the first one. A link sent to the wrong person can sit unopened for weeks.
sections.3.heading: Worked example: one invoice from a team in three cities
sections.3.paragraphs: Here is how a small consultancy might bill one project in a month. The figures are illustrative, not from a real customer. The partner works from London, and two consultants work remotely from Lisbon and Toronto. All three track time against the same client project in Paidlyo. | The project has two tasks with their own rates: strategy workshops at £150 an hour and research at £90 an hour. The client wants to see who did the work, so the invoice is grouped by person. On the first working day of the month, the partner opens the client, creates the invoice from unbilled time and checks the draft. | The subtotal is £6,660. The consultancy adds 20% tax, so the client is billed £7,992. The partner sends the link the same morning. Nobody had to email a timesheet, and nobody waited for a colleague in another time zone to wake up.
sections.3.bullets: Partner, strategy workshops: 12 hours at £150 = £1,800 | Consultant in Lisbon, research: 30 hours at £90 = £2,700 | Consultant in Toronto, research: 24 hours at £90 = £2,160 | Subtotal £6,660, plus 20% tax = £7,992
sections.4.heading: Questions to ask before you trust any online invoicing tool
sections.4.paragraphs: Moving billing online means a company outside your business holds your client list, your rates and your invoice history. That's normal for most software today, but it's worth asking a few plain questions before you commit, whichever tool you choose. | First, who in your team can see what? Paidlyo has three roles, owner, admin and member, so check which role each person needs before you invite them. Second, can you get your data out? In Paidlyo you can export hours, unbilled time and outstanding invoices to CSV whenever you like. Third, what do your clients see? With Paidlyo they see only the invoice behind the link you share, not your account. | Finally, think about what happens when there's no internet. Online software needs a connection, and Paidlyo has no offline mode or mobile app. If you often work without a connection, write your hours down and add them to the weekly timesheet later.
sections.4.bullets: Roles: decide who should handle billing and give the matching role | Export: check you can download your records as files | Client view: clients should see their invoice, not your whole account | Connection: online tools need internet, so plan for the times you're offline
sections.4.callout: A tool that makes it hard to export your data is a tool that's hard to leave. Check the export before you need it.
sections.5.heading: Moving your invoicing online from spreadsheets or Harvest
sections.5.paragraphs: If you invoice from spreadsheets today, start small. Add your active clients, their projects and the hourly rates for each project or task. Set each client's currency. Then ask the team to track time in Paidlyo from the first day of a new month, so the first invoice is built entirely from tracked hours. | Don't try to recreate old invoices. Keep the PDFs you've already sent where they are, and note any amounts clients still owe you so you can follow them up. After one billing cycle you'll know whether your rates and tasks are set up the way you want. | If you're coming from Harvest, you can import your data from a Harvest CSV export. Paidlyo shows you a preview first, and nothing is saved until you confirm it.
sections.5.bullets: Add active clients, projects and rates first | Set each client's currency before the first invoice | Start tracking on the first day of a month | Keep old invoices as PDFs and note open balances | Coming from Harvest: import the CSV and check the preview

faq.1.question: Do I need to install anything to use Paidlyo?
faq.1.answer: No. Paidlyo runs in a web browser, so you sign in and start working. There's nothing to download or update.
faq.2.question: Do my clients need an account to see their invoice?
faq.2.answer: No. Each invoice has a private link your client can open without signing up. They can save the invoice as a PDF from the same page.
faq.3.question: Is there a Paidlyo mobile app?
faq.3.answer: No. Paidlyo runs in a web browser and there's no mobile app or offline mode, so you need an internet connection to use it.
faq.4.question: Is Paidlyo free to use online?
faq.4.answer: There's no free plan. Paidlyo costs $9 per person a month, with every feature included. You can try it for 14 days first: a card is needed to start, but nothing is charged until the trial ends.
